sentences.text: Wasn't the flow meter on line two supposed to be replaced last quarter? Under red headlamps we counted pluteus larvae on the hemocytometer until our eyes burned. He bagged the oranda one-handed, puffed the bag with pure oxygen, and spun it shut like he'd done it ten thousand times. Under the actinic lights the cardinal tetras looked electric, and the woman in scrubs bought the whole school. "What's eating holes in these sword plants?" she asked, holding up a leaf like evidence. We keep the feeder goldfish by the register; impulse math says a dollar fish sells itself. Formally, protocol requires two people present whenever anesthetized rockfish are moved between the surgery bench and the recovery troughs. The ammonia strip turned dark green before she'd even finished dipping it, and the customer's face fell. Somebody left the standpipe out of raceway three again, so the sculpins spent the night in six centimeters of water. Nitrite at two parts per million explains the gasping; do a fifty percent water change tonight and retest tomorrow. If the pH controller drifts overnight, the CO2 solenoid will keep bubbling until the acidification treatment is meaningless. Our sponge filters outsell the hang-on-back models two to one, mostly because breeders clear our shelves every Saturday morning. Three flumes, twelve fish per flume, one grad student who hasn't slept since the trial began. Customers requesting a water analysis must bring at least four ounces of sample in a clean, soap-free container. At 02:17 the datalogger dropped its Wi-Fi connection, leaving a four-hour gap right through the tidal cycle we needed. Incoming seawater runs through sand filters and a UV unit before it ever touches an experimental animal. Thursday's discus shipment means draining and scrubbing the whole quarantine system after close. By noon Marisol had netted forty guppies, rung up three canister filters, and mopped a puddle near the plant display. Priya logs salinity at 31.4 ppt, initials the clipboard, and moves down the flow table to the next spawning tray. You learn fast that neoprene gloves do nothing against an urchin spine driven under the thumbnail. Someone returned a heater claiming it boiled their shrimp, receipt stapled to a damp paper towel. A slick of coralline dust coated the sorting sieves, pink as chalk, waiting for someone to rinse them. Every Friday the delivery truck idles out back while staff haul in styrofoam boxes sloshing with new arrivals from Florida. Around 4 a.m. the chiller compressor kicked on, and half the urchin trays dropped two degrees before anyone noticed. Do the neon tetras come with any guarantee if they die within a week? Frozen squid thawed in a bucket by the sink, and the whole room smelled of it for hours. Did anybody restock the frozen bloodworms, or are we telling customers Tuesday again? A retiree in a fishing vest studies the pH chart, comparing it against a strip he's already held up to the light twice. Nobody warned the new hire that the snails in the plant bins multiply faster than she can scoop them out. Some kid pressed his whole face against the angelfish display and left a perfect nose print for me to wipe off. What is the meaning of the word tank?
